task.title: Write text in a drawing
task.shortdesc: The text of a drawing is text in the PDF, with the fonts you choose. You can place it character by character, set it along a path, wrap it to a width or pour it into a shape.

info.p: A text element writes a line. Its x and y attributes give the point where the line starts. The y is the baseline, the line the letters stand on, so letters go above it. The properties font-family, font-size, font-weight and font-style, and the other font properties of Font selection and sizing, work as they do in the rest of the document. The text is painted with fill and stroke, like a shape.
The property text-anchor chooses which part of the line is at the point: start, the initial value, middle or end. Use middle to center a label on a point.
Spaces and line feeds in the text collapse, as they do in the rest of your document. Set xml:space="preserve", or white-space: pre, to keep them.

stepxmp.pre: <text x="10" y="30" font-size="20" fill="#222222">Plain <tspan fill="#8a2a2a" font-weight="bold">text</tspan> with a <tspan dy="-6" font-size="14" fill="#1d4f7a">raised</tspan><tspan dy="6"> word</tspan></text>

step.cmd: Change and move parts of a line

info.p: A tspan element is a part of the text with its own style or position. It can have all the attributes of text. These attributes place the characters:

ul.li: x and y set the position of characters. A list of numbers, such as x="10 30 50", sets one position for each of the first characters. The characters after the last number follow the previous one.
dx and dy move a character and the ones after it, by the lengths they give. They can be lists too.
rotate turns each character, by the angles of its list in degrees. The last angle is used for the rest of the characters.

info.p: The property baseline-shift raises or lowers a part of the line, with the values super and sub or a length. The property dominant-baseline chooses the baseline of the text that is placed at the y, such as middle or hanging.

The properties letter-spacing, word-spacing and text-decoration work as in the rest of your document. The attribute textLength gives the length that the text must have. The attribute lengthAdjust chooses how CSSMedia reaches it: spacing, the initial value, changes the space between characters, and spacingAndGlyphs stretches the characters too.

Put a textPath element inside a text element, and name a shape in its href. The text follows the outline of the shape. The attribute startOffset moves the start along the path, with a length or a percentage of the length of the path. With side="right" the text goes on the right side of the path, in the opposite direction.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <path id="curve" d="M10 150 C 50 90, 130 90, 170 150"/> </defs> <text font-size="16" fill="#1d4f7a"><textPath href="#curve" startOffset="10">Text that follows a path</textPath></text>

step.cmd: Wrap text to a width or into a shape

info.p: With the property inline-size on a text element, the text wraps to lines of that length. The line breaks follow the rules of the languages of the text. The property text-anchor aligns the lines in the length.

With the property shape-inside the text fills a shape. Each line is as long as the shape is wide at that height, and the text goes around the holes. The value is a basic shape, such as circle(), ellipse(), polygon() or inset(), a reference to a shape of the drawing, such as url(#id), or the URL of an image, whose opaque pixels are the area. In a shape, text-align aligns the lines, and text-align: justify makes them fill the width.

fig.title: A line, text on a path and text in a shape

image.alt: A line of text with a bold red word and a small raised blue word. Below it, blue text that follows an arch. On the right, a circle with a few lines of text inside it, which are shorter near the top and the bottom.

stepxmp.pre: <circle cx="260" cy="95" r="60" fill="#eef4fa" stroke="#1d4f7a"/> <text x="205" y="60" font-size="12" fill="#222222" style="shape-inside: circle(58px at 260px 95px)">Lines of this text are shorter near the top and the bottom of the circle that holds them.</text>

step.cmd: Write vertically or from right to left

info.p: The property writing-mode set to vertical-rl or vertical-lr writes the text in vertical lines, as in the languages of East Asia, and text-orientation chooses how its characters are turned. The property direction: rtl and the Unicode bidirectional algorithm write text from right to left where the language needs it.
